summary_raw: sqlite3_rsync: Database Remote-Copy Tool For SQLite This additional SQLite tool has been around for a while now - it was added as "experimental" in SQLite 3.47.0 in October 2024 and enhanced in SQLite 3.50.0 in May 2025 . Normally, if you want to grab a snapshot copy of a SQLite database, you need to use either the backup API or VACUUM INTO . title: Quoting Scott Aaronson
summary_raw: It’s now obvious that we’ll be getting, not one-off solutions to this or that complexity question, but a whole new continent of mathematical truth, one that we’d previously only glimpsed through fog. Picture van Leeuwenhoek first training a microscope on pondwater, or Galileo first training his telescope on the stars. That might give you some idea of how our resolution into the complexity-theoretic universe, and the whole universe of mathematical truth beyond it, has now improved. — Scott Aaronson Tags: mathematics , llms , ai , generative-ai

title: Amazon and Meta are in talks to end the block on Meta's AI shopping agent Muse in Amazon's online store.
summary_raw: Amazon and Meta are in talks to bring back Muse, Meta's AI shopping agent that Amazon kicked off its platform in September. The two sides are stuck on ad revenue and who gets to control search results. That matters because Amazon's ad business generates $68.6 billion a year, and Muse already commands 51 percent of all agentic shopping orders. title: AI agents now control part of Deepmind's compute for Gemini experiments, but recursive self-improvement remains distant
summary_raw: Google Deepmind uses AI agents to run experiments on their own for upcoming Gemini models. Research chief Koray Kavukcuoglu says the lab is still far from recursive self-improvement. For oversight, Deepmind intentionally leaves the agents' internal chains of thought untrained so they can be reviewed. Kavukcuoglu measures AGI by everyday user trust rather than benchmarks. title: Anthropic study shows the hardest part of adopting AI at work has little to do with learning the tools
summary_raw: Anthropic studied nearly 300 AI deployments across 58 US companies with sobering results. Nearly one in five still delivers no business value, held back by heavy review workloads, internal bottlenecks, and employee resistance. The researchers say the biggest hurdles stem from outdated company structures. title: MIT team discovers that unrealistic training data makes AI climate predictions more reliable
summary_raw: MIT researchers have developed a method that lets AI climate models get by with a single training run instead of the usual six to eight. An algorithm generates deliberately unrealistic scenarios with extreme CO2 or methane swings that make the model more robust. Until now, these emulators were often outdated by the time they were finished, according to the researchers.
